Kabc020235882018
 In The Court Of Xxi Addl.Small Cause Judge And
 Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore.

(Scch-23)

 Present: Sri. Shreyansh Doddamani
 B.Com. Ll.B (Spl)

(Policy No.VPV02361160001000)
 (Sri. V. Shrihari Naidu, Advocate)
JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners in the nutshell is that, on 01.08.2018, the deceased was going towards his village Seethappanahalli from Narasapura by observing all the traffic rules and regulations by riding a Royal Enfield Bullet Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-HK-8653.

On the way at about 8.30 p.m, when he reached near Indo Circle at Narasapura Industrial Area, on Narasapura - Malur Road,
Kolar Taluk and District, at that time one Tata Indica V2 car bearing Reg.No.KA-07-A-3349 was going ahead of the deceased's motorcycle in the same direction with high speed in a rash and negligent manner.

The driver of the said car all of a sudden applied brake negligently without giving any indication or signal and stopped the said car on the left side of the road as a result of which the rider of the Bullet motorcycle / deceased dashed against the rear portion of the Indica car.
Due to the terrific impact, the deceased sustained severe bodily injuries.
Immediately after the accident he was rushed to R.L. Jalappa Hospital, Kolar, he succumbed to the said injuries on the way to the hospital.
Postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to the family members, who conducted funeral and other ceremonies.
The respondent No.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer of the aforementioned Indica car are jointly & severally liable to pay compensation.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1.
Respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel, he failed to contest the matter by filing the written statement.
4. The respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel and filed written statement and also filed amended written statement by contending that the petition is not maintainable either law or on facts.

Further the respondent No.2 has contended that, the owner and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provision of 64-VB of Insurance Act and Sections 147, 149, 134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.
The respondent No.2 admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Car/ Taxi bearing Reg.No.KA-07-A-3349.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Negligence on the part of the driver of its insured car is denied by this respondent.

Per contra it is alleged that the deceased who was riding the motorcycle without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the road and without maintaining the distance between the vehicles in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and in the process of overtaking the car / taxi lost control over the vehicle and dashed against the rear portion of the offending car, fell down and sustained injuries and succumbed to the accident.

Hence the deceased was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident and it is a self accident of the Usha.M.R vs Jayaraj.K.N on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130869116/
2 deceased.
In fact deceased was also not wearing helmet and also not possessing valid DL at the time of alleged accident.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the car did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners prove that on 01.08.2018 at about 8.30 p.m, near Indo Circle, Narasapura - Malur road, Narasapura Industrial Area, Kolar Taluk and District, the driver of the Tata Indica V2 car bearing Reg.No.KA-07-A-3349 drove it rash and negligently and dashed the Royal Enfield Bullet motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05- HK-8653 and caused the death of this vehicle rider by name Sri.
Rajendra Prasad.

S.A? 
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation ? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3.
What order or award?
6. The Petitioner No.1 was examined as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 10 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
The petitioner has also examined the mother of the deceased as PW.2 and through her Ex.P.11 was marked.
An eye-witness to the accident in question : Sri.S.B. Vasantha Gowda was examined as PW.3.
Ex.P.12 was marked through him.

In order to prove its defence, the respondent No.2/Insurance company got examined its State Head Legal Department as RW.1.
7.
Heard erudite counsel for the petitioners and respondent counsels on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.
The counsel for petitioners relied on the decision reported in 2021 ACJ 2558, in the case of National Ins. Co.Ltd., V/s Chamundeshwari & others.

entities.text: National Ins. Co.Ltd., V/s Chamundeshwari & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : Partly in the affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1 : The uncle of the deceased set the criminal law into the motion by lodging Ex.P.2-First information statement.

Based on compliant, the jurisdictional police registered FIR as per Ex.P.1, investigated the matter and laid chargesheet (Ex.P.11) against the driver's of both vehicles involved in the accident for the offences punishable u/s's 279 and 304(A) of IPC.

Usha. M.R vs Jayaraj.K.N on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130869116/
3 9.
There is no dispute regarding the occurrence of the accident on the relevant date, time and place.
The death of the deceased due to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident is also not in conflict.
The only issue with which the parties are at loggerheads is with regard to the factum of negligence.
10. Initially the complaint lodged against driver of Tata Indica car as he dashed to the motorcycle of deceased on head on collusion by driving his car in rash and negligent manner.
Accordingly, the investigation officer conducted the Panchanama and prepared the sketch.
As per the damages it appears that, the accident was not head on collusion but it was the rider of the motorcycle dashed to the car on its rear side.
As per the charge sheet, the deceased who was rider of the motorcycle dashed to the moving car.
Admittedly it was public road and the road was more than 40 feet width.
In such circumstances, the car or four wheelers run minimum 50 km speed.
If deceased dashed the motorcycle to the moving car which was running minimum 50 km speed, the damages could be less to the car but as per the Ex.P5 IMV Report there are more damages to the car.
It clearly reveals that the driver of the car suddenly applied the brake then only the deceased who riding the bike dashed to the car.

As manifest from the police records and testimony of PW.1, the driver of Tata Indica car (which was proceeding ahead of the deceased motorcycle) applied the brakes suddenly without giving any indication.

Under such circumstances, it appears in all probability that by the time the rider of the motorcycle / deceased realized the said fact, it would have been too late for him to react and check or divert his vehicle to avoid collision.
What also deserves notice is that the accident occurred on a Junction road.
At the outset, the very act of the driver of the car drove the same in rash and negligent manner that too without giving any indication suddenly stopped the vehicle on the left side of the road.

Hence, despite putting best efforts the rider of the motorcycle could not have controlled his vehicle and thereby dashed against the car itself depicts that he did not exercise the degree of care which is expected of a prudent driver.
11. Further Regulation No.24 of the Rules of Road Regulations 1989 prescribes that 'No driver of a vehicle shall apply brake abruptly unless it is necessary to do so for safety reasons'.
In the present case nothing is placed on record to show that there was sufficient reason for the driver of the car to apply sudden brakes.

Even otherwise when the charge sheet is filed against the drivers of the both car and deceased for rash and negligent driving, burden was cast on the owner as well as insurer thereof to disprove the same.
Claimants cannot be called upon to prove a negative factor.
For the best reasons known to him, the owner of the car appeared before the court but he failed to contest the matter by filing written statement.
Accordingly an adverse inference could be drawn against him the he has impliedly admitted the petition averments.
Added to this the respondent No.2 did not make any attempt to examine the driver of its insured car who is the best witness to depose about the cause of accident.
There is no explanation to that effect.
Non-examination of the said driver is fatal to the defence of respondent No.2.
Hence, its contention that there was no negligence on the part of driver of car has to be disbelieved.

The driver of the car who had failed to adhere to the basic traffic rules & regulations and acted in a gross negligent manner without giving any indication suddenly stopped his vehicle had contributed a higher degree of negligence in the occurrence of the resultant accident.
In such circumstances on the basis of available records the only inference that can be drawn is that the drivers of both the vehicles were equally responsible for the occurrence of the accident.

Thereby the negligence attributed towards each of them is 60:40% (60 on driver of car Usha.M.R vs Jayaraj.K.N on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130869116/
4 and 40% on deceased i.e, rider of the motor cycle).

As such, I answer Issue No.1 as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
12. ISSUE NO.2 :
The petitioners claim that, petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 is the mother of the deceased.
To prove the same, petitioner No.1 filed affidavit-in- lieu of her chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Ration card and Aadhar cards marked at Ex's.P.8 to 10 and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
Further the PW.1 was not tendered for cross examination.
Therefore the evidence of PW.1 is not considerable.
Further the mother of the deceased is examined as PW.2.
In the cross examination PW.2 elicited that the deceased was residing with her.

Further she stated that after the death of deceased his wife /
petitioner No.1 got another marriage and she got married with another person within 3 to 4 months from the date of death and she has two children out of second marriage.
The deceased has no issues.
Further PW.2 stated that the PW.1 has given her evidence after second marriage.
This Court will not loose sight of the fact that, the petitioner No.2 is the mother of deceased Rajendra Prasad.
S.A. The evidence discloses that deceased is the son who is a one of the bread winner to the family and as such the petitioner No.2 was dependent on deceased.
It is pertinent to note that, this relationship of the petitioners with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondent No.2.

Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representative of the deceased.
Therefore, only petitioner No.2 is the legal heir and dependent of deceased.
13. In this case the petitioners have claimed the compensation of Rs.45,00,000/- on the death of deceased in the road traffic accident.
The petitioners contended that, deceased was working as mason and also an agriculturist and earning of Rs.25,000/-p.m.
To prove the income of the deceased, the petitioners have not produced any documents.
Be that as it may, in the absence of authentic proof of income of the deceased, this Tribunal has to consider his income notionally for calculating the compensation.
Admittedly the accident took place in the year 2018.
It is trite law that, when the petitioners have failed to prove the income, the income of the deceased has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
It is relevant to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV) dated.05.07.2023.

entities.text: Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
Usha.M.R vs Jayaraj.K.N on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130869116/
5
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred on 01.08.2018.
Therefore, Rs.12,500/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.

14. So far as the age of the deceased is concerned, the petitioners have produced the Aadhar card to show the age of the deceased as per Ex.P9 wherein the date of birth of deceased is shown as 21.12.1993, and the accident had taken place on 01.08.2018 and it shows that, at the time of accident the deceased was aged about 24 years.

Hence the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is '18'.
15.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 24 years.
Therefore, in this case, 40% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

Further as stated above that, as on the date of accident, deceased aged about 24 years and as such, 40% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.17,500/- p.m. (Rs.12,500/-
+ 5,000/- i.e. 40%).
16.
The deceased died living behind one dependent.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/3rd of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.11,667/- p.m. (Rs.17,500 - Rs.5,833 = Rs.11,667/-).
17.
The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.11,667/- p.m. and the multiplier '18' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.25,20,072/- (Rs.11,667/- X 12 X 18).
Considering the above facts, this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.25,20,000/- under the head of loss of dependency.

18. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners contended that they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc., but no documents are produced.
Hence, this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years.
By applying the observations made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years elapsed from the date of order amount of consortium, funeral expense and loss of estate to be enhanced.

19. In this case, the petitioner No.2 is the mother of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Usha.M.R vs Jayaraj.K.N on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130869116/
6 Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioner No.2 entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Usha.M.R vs Jayaraj.K.N
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of a son cause great shock and agony to the parents of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards deceased her son.
Therefore, petitioner No.2 is entitled for Rs.40,000/- under the head of Filial consortium.

20 . The calculation table stands as follows:
1 Loss of dependency : 25,20,000-00 2 Loss of consortium : - Nil - 3 Funeral Expenses & : 18,150-00 Transportation 4 Loss of Estate : 18,150-00 5
Towards loss of Filial consortium to : 40,000-00 petitioner No.2

Total :
25,96,300-00 Less 40% towards contributory : 10,38,520-00 negligence on the part of the deceased (Rs.25,96,300 - 10,38,520)

Total compensation awarded :
15,57,780-00 21.

REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY : Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
22. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of Tata Indica V2 car bearing Reg.No.KA-07-A-3349 and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.

However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest in the ratio of 60 :
40 within two months from the date of this order.

Accordingly issue No.2 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
23. ISSUE NO.3 : In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.15,57,780/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of Two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
Usha.M.R vs Jayaraj.K.N on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130869116/
7
Petitioner No.1 - Nil -  Petitioner No.2 - 100%

Out of the share amount of petitioner No.2 a sum equal to 25% shall be deposited in her name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 75% shall be released to her through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners No.2 is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer and printout taken by him, then corrected and pronounced by me in the open court on this the 4th day of October- 2024)
(Shreyansh Doddamani)
XXI Addl. Small Causes Judge & ACJM, Bengaluru.
